newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares end firmer, OTCs active.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares end firmer, OTCs active.

text.p: Singapore shares finished higher on Thursday with Malaysian over-the-counter (OTC) stocks leading active trading.

The UOB OTC tracking mainly Malaysian stocks rose slightly, up 0.99 points to 1,172.45 with Sungei Way and Samanda and Land & General among top gainers. There was talk of some programme buying of Malaysian shares, said one dealer. Stockbroking firm Rashid Hussain also rose 45 cents to S$6.25 on talk that the company was going to make a placement, said dealers.
Buying of selected bluechip counters pushed the key Straits Times Industrials Index was up 13.48 points to end at 2,116.44.
Total volume was 96.99 million units with 194 gainers against 128 losers.

A dealer said the light volume in Singapore blue chips belied a listless market where uptrend was limited. "The market is in a state of suspended animation. The music slowed down and nobody knows when it will stopped," he said.
Another dealer said: "It is an order-driven market. The index would probably trade in a straight line for a while yet."
Electro Resources chalked up 14.33 million shares with several block trades crossed at between S$1.40 and S$1.43.
